newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BALAKOV WILL BE THE MAN IN FOCUS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BALAKOV WILL BE THE MAN IN FOCUS.

text.p: Krassimir Balakov, VfB Stuttgart's inspirational playmaker, showed the fun-loving side of his character on a German television sports show when he took over the work of a cameraman during a live broadcast.
But when the Bulgarian international lines up for Stuttgart in Saturday's Bundesliga clash with Bayern Munich, the cameras will be focused on him and his attitude will be deadly serious.

"I've always tried to be as professional as possible," Balakov said. "Professionalism is a very high target and you can't achieve it 100 percent. But every player must want to come as close to that 100 percent as possible."
Balakov is the driving force behind Stuttgart's "magic triangle" of attacking players, slotting in behind strikers Fredi Bobic and Giovane Elber.
He has scored 13 league goals -- including some of the most memorable and spectacular by any player in the Bundesliga -- and set up 12 more for his team mates this season.
Balakov joined Stuttgart in 1995 from Sporting Lisbon. But he has not forgotten his early days as a player with Etar Tarnovo in communist Bulgaria.
"We all dreamed of playing in the sort of professional conditions that existed in Germany, Italy, Spain or Portugal," he said.

"When I joined the professionals at the age of 16, I had to clean the older players' shoes and was only allowed to take a shower after them," he recalled. "I earned practically nothing as a player. I played for the love of football."
Although Balakov is now one of the Bundesliga's big earners, his love of the game is still obvious.
He makes no secret of his dislike for the more defensive style of football which has become the trademark of his opponents on Saturday under coach Giovanni Trapattoni.
"Bayern's football is not the sort I like. I love football which is attractive and fun to play," he said. "Here in Stuttgart I can play football the way I always wanted to."

Although Stuttgart are now out of the running for this season's title, Balakov is confident the club will be a force to be reckoned with in the coming seasons. He has already extended his contract until the year 2000.
"If players and officials don't make mistakes we'll be as strong as Bayern or Dortmund in a couple of years," he said.
